summary.one_liner: A collection of documented WSL2 + Windows Terminal fixes for Claude Code, covering screenshot paste, Windows balloon notifications, LSP wiring, a usage-aware statusline, and related bridge utilities.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a set of markdown guides, each describing one fix for running Claude Code under WSL2 with Windows Terminal. Image-paste uses a systemd user service that keeps wsl-screenshot-cli running and saves screenshots under /tmp/.wsl-screenshot-cli/ so a copied Windows screenshot can be pasted as a WSL path. Claude-notify shows a Windows balloon tip on Claude Code Notification events and skips it when Windows Terminal is focused, and codex-notify reuses that script for Codex's notify command. Other guides cover LSP plugins and language servers for TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust, a statusline showing project, git branch, context fill and 5-hour/7-day usage, terminal tab titles, Shift+Enter newline handling, opening links in the Windows browser, and CapsLock-to-Escape via SharpKeys. A bin/tmux-notify-run script runs detached tmux jobs with logs and a Windows completion notification, and scripts/doctor.sh gives a read-only report of installed pieces and known conflicts. The author notes the setup is no longer tested daily on WSL2.
use_cases: paste Windows screenshots into Claude Code on WSL2
get Windows notifications when Claude Code finishes or needs permission
set up language servers for code navigation in Claude Code
show context window and usage in a Claude Code statusline
open OAuth and browser links from WSL2 in the Windows browser
run long tmux jobs with Windows completion alerts
how_to_run: Prompt Claude with: Help me set up this repository's WSL2 features. Check my environment, explain the changes, and preserve my existing settings.
notable: Each fix is documented with root cause and exact configuration, including non-obvious steps
Screenshot paste via a Go-based daemon that writes shots to WSL paths
Windows balloon notifications on Claude Code hooks, suppressed when Windows Terminal has focus
Statusline with context-window fill bar and color-coded 5-hour and 7-day usage
scripts/doctor.sh flags known conflicts such as duplicate screenshot monitors
caveats: Targets WSL2 with Windows Terminal; Windows-side behavior needs manual changes and is not tested daily by the author
Maintenance status: the author moved to Ubuntu + Ghostty and no longer tests this setup daily
Some steps require changes on the Windows side, such as SharpKeys registry remap and balloon scripts
